title: Publish the customer snapshot bucket in the CloudFormation template
description:
**Phase 1 of 5.**

- **Blocked by:** nothing required to start — sequence with other customer-visible template edits. `chatticus-82dab7c4-a44c-4e0e-ac19-51a0c7a12d09` is closed (customer `ChatticusComputers` + lab-user `RunTask`).
- **Does not unblock** agent file actions. Under the dict branch of `chatticus-fccc4e9a-b3c6-4a14-9317-d0b0c95231b7` it **never will**. File-row evidence still lives on `chatticus-3e72dc16-ff6f-44f2-8d3c-dd3a49f9ac52`.

> **Verified 2026-09-07 against `infra/customer-role.yml`:** the role has **no `s3:` permissions of any kind** (`grep -c 's3:'` → 0). That is why a **host pack** cannot be published or hydrated today. It is **not** why `read_workspace` is empty — that tool hits an in-process dict Dynamo does not persist.

> CloudFormation creates resources with the **caller's** permissions. Declaring the bucket inside a Chatticus-deployed `ChatticusComputers` stack would still require `s3:CreateBucket` on the role. Putting it in the **customer-run published template** is the only option that keeps bucket creation off the Anthus role entirely.

---

## Why this card still exists (insurance, not file-actions)

Building the bucket early is cheap insurance. Template changes are customer-visible, and there are no customers yet. By `chatticus-8a25af4a-7ae7-44e6-8229-e1d8313b712b`'s rule, changing the published template means an existing customer has to re-run it. Free today, expensive after beta.

**Stop describing this as unblocking file actions.** Agent `read_workspace` / `write_workspace` touch `computer.workspace` (the dict). Nothing in the agent loop writes host `workspace/` or `browser-profiles/`. `ComputerHostDisk` packs those trees in tests/CLI; the Fargate host worker never publishes or hydrates. Creating the bucket does not connect that wire.

If the product chooses **host disk**, this bucket is where packs live and the role later needs `s3:Get`/`s3:Put` on the named bucket (still not `s3:CreateBucket`). If it chooses the **dict as a deliberate placeholder**, this bucket stores something no agent tool writes — still worth declaring now so we are not asking customers to re-run a template later.

## Decision (2026-09-07) — which account holds packs

**Snapshot packs live in the customer's own AWS account, and the bucket is created in advance by the published CloudFormation template.**

Anthus keeps its shared `ChatticusSnapshots` bucket for **Anthus-managed organizations only**. A customer organization's `/workspace` and browser-profile packs never rest in an Anthus-owned bucket.

That is the pitch claim — *their files, their account* — made literal for **host packs**. It is only *operative* for agents if tools are wired to host disk (open decision; do not pick it here).

## Why the template, not the assumed role

1. **The customer can read what they are agreeing to.** `chatticus-8a25af4a-7ae7-44e6-8229-e1d8313b712b`: *"the people with authority to grant this will read the policy."* A bucket in the template is reviewable before they run it.
2. **Chatticus never needs `s3:CreateBucket`.** Granting write access to one named bucket is a narrower ask.
3. **No first-run race.** The bucket exists before the first hydrate or publish.
4. **Clean teardown.** Encryption, versioning, and block-public-access are declared and theirs. `Retain` is the safer `DeletionPolicy` default.

## Design target, not shipping

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (`4142832`) calls the S3 snapshot protocol the **design target. It is not currently wired.** Do not cite the earlier "shipping design" / "load-bearing" wording (`48a2c79`). `chatticus-fbae4eb4-df8d-42ab-af4a-2f9f0911b516` still holds as the *target* under the host-disk branch: `/workspace` stays on host-local disk; do not delete the snapshot library; no `/workspace` EFS.

## Open sub-questions to settle while writing it

- **Naming.** S3 names are globally unique. `OrganizationId` (the `tenant_id` UUID) is already a template parameter.
- **`DeletionPolicy`.** `Retain` unless Ryan picks otherwise.
- **Region.** Same region as the organization computer, or every hydrate/publish pays cross-region.
- **Encryption and access.** SSE, versioning, block-public-access in the template.
- **Path layout.** `docs/COMPUTER_SNAPSHOTS.md` specifies `s3://…/tenants/{tenant_id}/computers/{computer_id}/`. One bucket per org may make the `tenants/` prefix redundant.

## Done when

The published template creates the snapshot bucket, the role is scoped to read/write that named bucket, `docs/COMPUTER_SNAPSHOTS.md` and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` record which account holds packs for which kind of organization, and the change is recorded as customer-visible. Do **not** claim this unblocks today's `read_workspace`.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
## What this bucket would hold is not what `read_workspace` reads (2026-09-07)

Verified: agent `read_workspace` / `write_workspace` touch `computer.workspace` (in-process dict). Dynamo does not persist it. The pack library (`ComputerHostDisk`) tars **host filesystem** `workspace/` + `browser-profiles/`. Nothing in the agent loop writes those trees. `ControlPlane.publish_snapshot` copies the dict for in-memory Gherkin.

**Decision, not assumption:** this card's bucket is for **host snapshot packs** (ARCHITECTURE / COMPUTER_SNAPSHOTS — "their files" on disk + Chromium profile). It is **not** a store for the control-plane dict, and it does **not** unblock `ls /workspace` or today's `read_workspace`. Bridging agent tools to host disk is product work, not implied by creating the bucket.

`chatticus-3e72dc` file-actions is therefore not blocked on this card the way terminal is not blocked on RunTask.
